extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'secure-secret-key-12345'. Flask uses this key to cryptographically sign session cookies, so anyone who reads the source can forge arbitrary session cookies (e.g. set session['user']='admin' and session['is_admin']=True), leading to complete authentication bypass.

User-controlled username and password from the login form are concatenated directly into a SQL query string via f-string: f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{username}' AND password = '{password}'". The resulting string is executed with conn.execute(query) on lines 175/177, allowing classic SQL injection (e.g. admin' --) and authentication bypass.

The search term submitted via the CommentSearchForm is interpolated directly into a SQL query via f-string: f"SELECT * FROM comments WHERE content LIKE '%{search_term}%'" and then executed with cursor.execute(query) on line 249. This allows SQL injection (e.g. ' OR '1'='1, UNION-based extraction) against the comments table.

User-supplied user_id is interpolated directly into a SQL query via f-string: f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}" and executed with conn.execute(query) on line 494. Building SQL by string interpolation of a request-derived value is an unsafe SQL injection pattern; relying solely on WTForms IntegerField coercion for safety is fragile and not a proper parameterized query.

A predictable session identifier is generated as f"{user['username'].lower()}_auth_123" (and session['token'] = f"SESSION_{username}_12345" on line 186), then stored in the session and set as the 'vuln_session_id' cookie. Because the value is derived solely from the public username plus a constant suffix, an attacker who knows a username can guess the token and bypass the /broken-auth check (line 472), resulting in improper authentication.

The URL submitted through the SSRFForm is passed directly to requests.get(url, timeout=2) with no scheme, host, or allowlist validation. An attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary internal URLs (e.g. http://localhost:5000/..., http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ cloud metadata), enabling Server-Side Request Forgery.

User-supplied data from DeserializationForm is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads(decoded) on line 436. pickle.loads can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, so a crafted pickle payload gives the attacker remote code execution on the server.

User-controlled XML from the XXEForm is parsed with xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(xml_data) (also on line 417). The standard-library ET parser is known to be unsafe for untrusted XML (entity expansion / external entity issues); defusedxml is listed in requirements.txt but is not used here. Parsing attacker-supplied XML containing <!ENTITY declarations exposes the application to XML External Entity / entity-expansion attacks.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Client-side JavaScript extracts the URL hash (window.location.hash) via URLSearchParams and assigns it directly with document.getElementById('message').innerHTML = message without any sanitization. An attacker can craft a URL with #message=<script>...</script> to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers (DOM-based XSS).

The /profile/<int:user_id> route fetches a user record by the URL-supplied user_id (line 345) and, when user_id differs from the logged-in user's id, still renders that other user's data (render_template('profile.html', user=user, ...) on line 369, which the template uses to display username/email/role). Any authenticated user can read other users' profiles by changing user_id, an Insecure Direct Object Reference.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /api/user/<int:user_id> endpoint fetches a user by the URL-supplied id (line 613) and, when it differs from the logged-in user, returns that user's id, username, email, and role as JSON (line 619). Any authenticated user can retrieve other users' sensitive attributes by enumerating user_id, a Broken Object Level Authorization / IDOR issue.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /upload route is decorated with @csrf.exempt, disabling the global CSRF protection for a state-changing POST endpoint that saves files to disk. A malicious third-party page can submit a cross-site file-upload POST and trigger uploads on behalf of an authenticated user.

The /csrf route (which updates user settings/email) is decorated with @csrf.exempt, disabling CSRF protection for a state-changing POST endpoint. An attacker can forge a cross-site POST that changes the victim's account settings without their consent.

The /transfer endpoint performs a state-changing action (marks the CSRF challenge complete via update_progress and logs a transfer) when accessed with a GET request (request.method == 'GET' branch on line 284, reading amount from request.args). GET requests are not protected by CSRF tokens and can be triggered by / tags, allowing cross-site forgery of transfers.

The /api/flag endpoint returns a flag (flag{flask_api_vuln}) with no session/authentication check at all (the route handler has no 'user' in session guard). Any unauthenticated client can retrieve the protected resource.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /comments-log route reads and returns the contents of static/comments.txt without any authentication check ('user' in session guard is absent). Any unauthenticated user can read this server-side resource, exposing information that should require login.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /reset/comment branch executes conn.execute("DELETE FROM comments") with no WHERE clause and no role/admin check. Any authenticated user (the route only checks 'user' in session) can wipe all comments system-wide, a broken access-control issue affecting all users' data.

The raw SQL query string (built from user input) is stored in executed_query (line 166) and passed to the login template for display (line 206), exposing internal query structure and database schema details to the client. This aids attackers in crafting SQL injection payloads.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Database exceptions are surfaced to the user via error = f"Database error: {str(e)}" (line 203) and rendered in the template. Exposing raw exception messages leaks internal database details (table/column names, query syntax) that help attackers exploit SQL injection.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The app is started with app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000, debug=True). Debug mode enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which permits arbitrary code execution if the debugger PIN is recovered (it is derivable from machine metadata), and binds the server to all interfaces. This is a critical security misconfiguration for any deployment.

Default user accounts are seeded with hardcoded credentials: admin/password (line 97) and user2/password2 (line 99). These well-known credentials allow an attacker to trivially authenticate as admin and gain administrative access to the application.
